alternates.speaker: Tulsidas (narrating)
alternates.setting: After Ram leaves for the forest, his mother Kausalya keeps his childhood things.
alternates.sanskrit: जननी निरखति बान-धनुहियाँ। बार-बार उर नैननि लावति प्रभुजूकी ललित पनहियाँ॥ कबहुँ प्रथम ज्यों जाइ जगावति कहि प्रिय बचन सँवारे। उठहु तात! बलि मातु बदनपर, अनुज-सखा सब द्वारे॥
alternates.line: She held his little shoes to her heart, and some mornings still went to wake him.
alternates.translation: The mother gazes at his little bow and arrows. Again and again she presses the Lord's small, lovely shoes to her heart and eyes. Sometimes, as before, she goes to wake him with tender words: "Get up, my child, your mother adores your face; your brothers and friends are all at the door."

alternates.speaker: the gopis
alternates.setting: The women of Braj, after Krishna has left, on missing him.
alternates.sanskrit: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥
alternates.line: "Since he left, it has been monsoon in our eyes."
alternates.translation: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
alternates.why: Tears for someone you miss are allowed.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

why: Two sources of the mind's pain (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Ashma Gita))

verse.ref: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles – Fourth Series, CLVI, p. 493
verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.listener: Mary Hale, whose father had just died
verse.setting: Condolence letter, 20 February 1900: a friend who has known many losses offers to carry hers.
verse.line: if it were possible to exchange grief, and had I a cheerful mind, I would exchange mine for your grief ever and always.
verse.translation: You have had shelter all your life. I was in the glare, burning and panting all the time. Now for a moment you have caught a glimpse of the other side. My life is made up of continuous blows like that, and hundred times worse, because of poverty, treachery, and my own foolishness! Pessimism! You will understand it, how it comes. Well, well, what shall I say to you, Mary? You know all the talks; only I say this and it is true — if it were possible to exchange grief, and had I a cheerful mind, I would exchange mine for your grief ever and always. Mother knows best.

why: the griever is not alone
someone would carry it with you

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Lecture 'Work and Its Secret', Los Angeles, 4 January 1900. On those who avoid pain by never loving.
verse.line: the man who never loves, who is hard and stony, escaping most of the miseries of life, escapes also its joys.
verse.translation: Therefore the man who never loves, who is hard and stony, escaping most of the miseries of life, escapes also its joys.
verse.why: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

prasang.title: Work and its secret (Los Angeles, 1900)
prasang.summary: His greatest lesson, he says, was to attend to the means as much as the end. Most failures come from neglecting the means, and most sorrow from clinging to what is already failing. Weakness invites misery, yet a heart that refuses to love also loses life's joys.
prasang.lesson: Look after the means; keep the power to let go.

why: the urge to shut down is answered
the pain is the other side of having loved, and the alternative was stone

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: How a householder becomes a 'world' for others.
verse.sanskrit: यन्मनुष्यान्वासयते यदेभ्योऽशनं ददाति तेन मनुष्याणामथ यत्पशुभ्यस्तृणोदकं विन्दति तेन पशूनां यदस्य गृहेषु श्वापदा वयाꣳस्या पिपीलिकाभ्य उपजीवन्ति तेन तेषां लोको
verse.line: Feed people, find water for animals; when even ants live off your home, you become a world for them.
verse.translation: By housing people and giving them food, he becomes a world for people. By finding grass and water for animals, he becomes a world for animals. When beasts, birds and even ants live off his house, he becomes a world for them.

why: the care reaches down to birds and ants
a household is seen as something many lives rest on

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
verse.translation: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Bearing passing discomfort is not putting up with harm or abuse; those are not weather to wait out.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

why: Feelings come and go, bear them; your wisdom is asleep, not gone (Lakshmana to Rama).
bearing what passes without being moved

story.title: Hanuman reaches Sita
story.story_hook: A ring fell out of the tree onto Sita's lap, and it had Ram's name on it.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram's message to Sita, carried across the sea by Hanuman.
verse.sanskrit: कहेहू तें कछु दुख घटि होई। काहि कहौं यह जान न कोई॥ तत्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा। जानत प्रिया एकु मनु मोरा ॥
verse.line: Speaking of pain lightens it. But whom can I tell? No one knows this ache.
verse.translation: Telling one's grief lightens it a little. But whom can I tell? No one knows this pain. The truth of the love between you and me, my beloved, only my own heart knows.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on those who miss him and those who know him.
verse.sanskrit: इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत । सर्वभूतानि संमोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप ॥
verse.line: From the pull of want and push of dislike comes the confusion that traps every being.
verse.translation: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, arising from desire and aversion, Bharata, all beings fall into confusion at birth, scorcher of enemies.
verse.why: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.

prasang.title: Those who miss the Lord and those who know him
prasang.summary: The deluded see only the outer form; desire and aversion confuse all beings. Those freed from confusion come to know the divine fully.
prasang.lesson: Pull and push of like and dislike are what confuse us.

why: The confusion of opposites (Bhagavad Gita 7.27)
confusion is the common starting condition, produced by liking and disliking

verse.speaker: Sugriva
verse.setting: Newly bound in friendship, Sugriva tells Ram what a friend means to him.
verse.sanskrit: आढ्यो वापि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा। निर्दोषश्च सदोषश्च वयस्यः परमा गतिः॥
verse.line: Rich or poor, happy or sad, flawed or not, a friend is your greatest refuge.
verse.translation: Rich or poor, happy or unhappy, faultless or flawed, a friend is one's greatest refuge.
verse.why: Two people in trouble can carry each other.

prasang.title: Ram and Sugriva's friendship
prasang.summary: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.
prasang.story_hook: Two exiles, each robbed of his wife and home, swore friendship over a fire.
prasang.lesson: Two people in trouble can carry each other.

why: Find the friend; trees that stand together hold each other up.
a friend is named as refuge in every condition

verse.speaker: Sanatkumara
verse.setting: A step in Sanatkumara's ladder: faith rests on steadiness, steadiness on action.
verse.sanskrit: यदा वै करोत्यथ निस्तिष्ठति नाकृत्वा निस्तिष्ठति कृत्वैव निस्तिष्ठति कृतिस्त्वेव विजिज्ञासितव्येति कृतिं भगवो विजिज्ञास इति ॥
verse.line: Steadiness comes from doing. No one becomes steady without acting; act, and steadiness follows.
verse.translation: When one acts, one becomes steadfast. One does not become steadfast without acting; only by acting does one become steadfast. So action itself must be understood. 'Sir, I wish to understand action.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

why: steadiness is built by the doing itself
Narada: learned and still grieving

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the inner happiness of one who sees clearly.
verse.sanskrit: शक्नोतीहैव यः सोढुं प्राक्शरीरविमोक्षणात् । कामक्रोधोद्भवं वेगं स युक्तः स सुखी नरः ॥
verse.line: Whoever can ride out the surge of desire and anger, here and now, is steady and happy.
verse.translation: One who is able, here in this life, before leaving the body, to withstand the surge born of desire and anger, is disciplined; he is a happy person.
verse.why: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

prasang.title: The yoga of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna describes the wise: equal-eyed towards all beings, not elated or crushed, finding joy within, seeing that sense pleasures end in sorrow, and able to withstand desire and anger.
prasang.lesson: Pleasures that start and end can't hold your happiness; find the joy within.

why: Whoever can withstand the surge of desire and anger here is happy.
the capacity to hold steady while the surge passes

story.title: Kunti watches her sons and daughter-in-law walk into exile
story.story_hook: She was too old to go with them. She stood at the gate and said one thing to her daughter-in-law, and then she wept.
story.summary: Kunti is too old for the forest, so Vidura will keep her in his house. She watches her five sons leave in deerskins, heads down, mocked by Duhshasana. Draupadi comes to take her leave in a single stained garment with her hair loose.
story.lesson: A parent's part, when the children must go, is to bless them truthfully and bear the waiting.
story.teaser: She was too old to go with them. She stood at the gate and said one thing to her daughter-in-law, and then she wept.

verse.speaker: Narada
verse.setting: Narada, master of every science, comes to Sanatkumara.
verse.sanskrit: सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मविच्छ्रुतꣳ ह्येव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्यस्तरति शोकमात्मविदिति सोऽहं भगवः शोचामि तं मा भगवाञ्छोकस्य पारं तारयत्विति तꣳ होवाच यद्वै किंचैतदध्यगीष्ठा नामैवैतत् ॥
verse.line: I have learned so much, yet I am sad. I know words, not myself. Help me cross this sorrow.
verse.translation: 'Sir, I know only the texts; I do not know the self. I have heard from people like you that one who knows the self crosses beyond sorrow. I am in sorrow, sir. Please take me across.' He said to him: 'Whatever you have studied is only name.'
verse.why: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

prasang.title: Narada: learned but sad
prasang.summary: Narada, who has mastered every science of his day, comes to Sanatkumara and admits he is unhappy: he knows words, not himself. Sanatkumara leads him step by step from names up through action and joy to the infinite, teaching that happiness is found only in the vast, never in the small.
prasang.story_hook: Narada knew every subject worth knowing, and still came to Sanatkumara feeling sad.
prasang.lesson: Success and learning don't cure sadness; only the infinite does.

why: 'I am in sorrow, sir', said by the most learned man of his age
I have learned so much and I am still sad. I know the words, not myself. Can you get me across this?

verse.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verse.setting: Garuda's last question is about the diseases of the mind; Kakbhushundi answers.
verse.sanskrit: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥
verse.line: Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.
verse.translation: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verse.why: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

prasang.title: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

why: The illnesses of the mind (Ramcharitmanas, Uttar Kand 121-122 (Gita Press))
the many pains are given one root

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.sanskrit: यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मैवाभूद्विजानतः । तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतः ॥
verse.line: When you see the same life in everyone, where is there room for confusion or grief?
verse.translation: For the one who knows, in whom all beings have become the self, what confusion, what sorrow can there be, seeing oneness everywhere?
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

why: nothing is finally apart from oneself
confusion has no footing where everything is known as one self

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna tells Arjuna where the divine is found.
verse.sanskrit: ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥
verse.line: The divine lives in the heart of every being, yours included.
verse.translation: The Lord dwells in the heart of every being, Arjuna, moving all beings by his power as if mounted on a machine.
verse.misuse: The second half is about nature moving us, not fatalism or excusing harm; use the first half as the card.

he is present within every being

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.
verse.sanskrit: चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः । बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ॥
verse.line: Inwardly hand all your work to the divine, hold it as your goal, and keep your mind on it.
verse.translation: Mentally resigning all actions to me, holding me as the highest, relying on the yoga of understanding, keep your mind always on me.
verse.why: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

prasang.title: Action with devotion: surrender
prasang.summary: Krishna urges Arjuna to offer all action, warns that ego will only trip him, tells him to reflect fully and then choose, and finally to take refuge in him alone and not grieve.
prasang.lesson: Reflect fully, choose freely, and set down the fear.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन । सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं सः योगी परमो मतः ॥
verse.line: Feel others' joy and pain as if they were your own. That is the highest practice.
verse.translation: One who, by comparison with himself, sees the same everywhere, Arjuna, whether in pleasure or in pain, is considered the highest yogi.

words.en: by comparison to the true self

verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

story.title: Jatayu's last fight and Ram's grief
story.story_hook: He was old and half-blind, and he flew at Ravana's chariot anyway.
story.summary: Ram returns to an empty hut and searches the forest, asking birds and trees if they have seen Sita. He finds the old vulture Jatayu dying; he had fought Ravana alone to stop the abduction. Ram tells him that for one whose heart is set on others' good, nothing is out of reach, and performs his funeral rites himself, as a son would.
story.lesson: Standing up for someone matters, even when you cannot win.
